   5: TinyXML-2 is a simple, small, efficient, C++ XML parser that can be

  16: ## What it does.
  17: 
  18: In brief, TinyXML-2 parses an XML document, and builds from that a
  19: Document Object Model (DOM) that can be read, modified, and saved.
  20: 
  21: XML stands for "eXtensible Markup Language." It is a general purpose
  36: TinyXML-2 is designed to be easy and fast to learn. It is one header and
  37: one cpp file. Simply add these to your project and off you go.
  38: There is an example file - `xmltest.cpp` - to get you started.
  39: 
  40: TinyXML-2 is released under the ZLib license,
  41: so you can use it in open source or commercial code. The details
  43: 
  44: TinyXML-2 attempts to be a flexible parser, but with truly correct and
  45: compliant XML output. TinyXML-2 should compile on any reasonably C++
  46: compliant system. It does not rely on exceptions, run-time type information,
  47: or the C++ Standard Library.
  48: 
  57: ## TinyXML-1 vs. TinyXML-2
  58: 
  59: TinyXML-2 has long been the focus of all development. It is well tested 
  60: and should be used instead of TinyXML-1.
  61: 
  62: TinyXML-2 uses a similar API to TinyXML-1 and the same
  63: rich test cases. But the implementation of the parser is completely re-written
  64: to make it more appropriate for use in a game. It uses less memory, is faster,
  65: and uses far fewer memory allocations.
  66: 
  67: TinyXML-2 has no dependency on the C++ Standard Library, and does not adapt or use any
 151: whitespace between elements.

 153: `PEDANTIC_WHITESPACE` is a new mode and not as tested as the other whitespace modes.

import os, subprocess, shutil, sys, time
root=r'C:\Users\12159\AppData\Local\Temp\ai_exec_benchmark\trial_ai_exec_02'
make=shutil.which('mingw32-make')
gpp=shutil.which('g++')
if not (make and gpp):
    raise SystemExit('Required existing MinGW tools not found')

def run(cmd, timeout=180):
    print('> ' + subprocess.list2cmdline(cmd))
    p=subprocess.run(cmd,cwd=root,text=True,encoding='utf-8',errors='replace',stdout=subprocess.PIPE,stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,timeout=timeout)
    lines=p.stdout.splitlines()
    # concise output: all if short, otherwise tail
    if len(lines)<=30:
        print(p.stdout.rstrip())
    else:
        print(f'... ({len(lines)-25} lines omitted) ...')
        print('\n'.join(lines[-25:]))
    print('exit:',p.returncode)
    return p

clean=run([make,'clean'])
if clean.returncode!=0:
    print('Clean failed; continuing with a fresh named output fallback if needed.')
build=run([make,'all','CXX='+gpp])
exe_candidates=[os.path.join(root,'xmltest.exe'),os.path.join(root,'xmltest')]
exe=next((p for p in exe_candidates if os.path.isfile(p)),None)
if build.returncode!=0 or not exe:
    print('Make build did not produce the test executable; falling back to direct compilation with the same MinGW compiler.')
    exe=os.path.join(root,'xmltest.exe')
    build=run([gpp,'-D_FILE_OFFSET_BITS=64','-O2','-Wall','-Wextra',os.path.join(root,'tinyxml2.cpp'),os.path.join(root,'xmltest.cpp'),'-o',exe])
if build.returncode!=0 or not os.path.isfile(exe):
    raise SystemExit('BUILD_FAILED')
print(f'executable: {exe} ({os.path.getsize(exe)} bytes)')
test=run([exe],timeout=180)
summary=[l for l in test.stdout.splitlines() if 'Fail' in l or 'Pass' in l]
print('detected summary:', summary[-1] if summary else '<none>')
if test.returncode!=0 or not any('Fail 0' in l for l in summary):
    raise SystemExit('TEST_FAILED')
print('BUILD_AND_TEST_OK')

def safe(s): return s.encode('gbk','backslashreplace').decode('gbk','replace')
def run(cmd, timeout=180):
    print(safe('> '+subprocess.list2cmdline(cmd)))
    p=subprocess.run(cmd,cwd=root,text=True,encoding='utf-8',errors='replace',stdout=subprocess.PIPE,stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,timeout=timeout)
    lines=p.stdout.splitlines()
    shown=lines if len(lines)<=30 else (['... (%d lines omitted) ...'%(len(lines)-25)]+lines[-25:])
    print(safe('\n'.join(shown)))
    print('exit:',p.returncode)
    return p

# Clean may already have run in the prior attempt; run it once more deterministically.
clean=run([make,'clean'])
build=run([make,'all','CXX='+gpp])
exe=next((p for p in [os.path.join(root,'xmltest.exe'),os.path.join(root,'xmltest')] if os.path.isfile(p)),None)
compile_cmd=[make,'all','CXX='+gpp]
if build.returncode!=0 or not exe:
    exe=os.path.join(root,'xmltest.exe')
    compile_cmd=[gpp,'-D_FILE_OFFSET_BITS=64','-O2','-Wall','-Wextra','tinyxml2.cpp','xmltest.cpp','-o','xmltest.exe']
    build=run(compile_cmd)
if build.returncode!=0 or not exe or not os.path.isfile(exe): raise SystemExit('BUILD_FAILED')
print('executable:',os.path.basename(exe),'bytes:',os.path.getsize(exe))
test=run([exe],timeout=180)
summary=[l for l in test.stdout.splitlines() if 'Fail' in l or 'Pass' in l]
print(safe('detected summary: '+(summary[-1] if summary else '<none>')))
if test.returncode!=0 or not any('Fail 0' in l for l in summary): raise SystemExit('TEST_FAILED')
print('BUILD_AND_TEST_OK')
